title: Fixed-Wing Flight Control Law Design using Incremental Control
relevance: Full doctoral thesis on fixed-wing flight-control design. Its Appendix A.3 reproduces the 2024 paper “Practical System Identification and Incremental Control Design for a Subscale Fixed-Wing Aircraft” (DOI 10.3390/act13040130), which reports actual sine-sweep system identification and closed-loop validation on the modified 1.3 m-span X-UAV Mini Talon “Albadrone.” IMU/GPS/pitot measurements, Hall-sensor surface/servo positions, and injected/controller commands are separately described; onboard logging is reported at 100 Hz. The Hall-sensor surface-position channels are measured rather than inferred from RC commands.
limitations: Research-modified platform with reported 1–2 kg weight range. This is a control-oriented local model and actuator study, not a complete nonlinear aerodynamic coefficient set or broad-envelope validation. The embedded article says its dataset is available on request; raw flight logs are not publicly bundled. The acquired original is the full 2025 doctoral thesis, not a standalone copy of the embedded 2024 journal article; the thesis has no DOI established here.
access: open-author-copy-downloaded; embedded 2024 article full text reproduced in Appendix A.3
license: The reproduced article states Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY); separate thesis license not stated in retained PDF
read_depth: Full 176-page thesis inspected and embedded 33-page 2024 article reviewed; model, instrumentation, data availability and flight-test sections checked

title: Load spectra of a light unmanned aircraft – data recording frequencies and resulting measurement variations
relevance: Reports two real Sky Surfer 2000 flights: a 7 min 25 s manually piloted maneuvering flight and a 12 min 29 s mostly-autonomous photogrammetry flight. A separate Logomatic v2 recorder sampled an added three-axis accelerometer and wing-deflection extensometer at 500 Hz; the analysis compares load-factor time histories/load spectra with autopilot IMU data and decimated 50 Hz and 5 Hz records. Aircraft details include 2.0 m span and reported 2.2 kg flying weight. This provides aircraft-specific measured normal-load behavior and a concrete sampling/aliasing caution.
limitations: This is a load-spectrum and structural-fatigue measurement study, not a six-degree-of-freedom aerodynamic/system-identification dataset. Load factor is computed from acceleration/extensometer signals, rather than direct force measurement; pilot/autopilot commands and actual control-surface positions are not the studied channels. Only plots and derived summaries are published; no downloadable raw flight log or data DOI was found.
access: publisher open-access PDF downloaded; full text inspected
license: CC BY 4.0 (stated in article)
read_depth: Full 21-page article inspected; airframe and sensor configuration, flight scenarios, signals, sampling rates and limitations checked

title: The Longitudinal Handling Characteristics of the Skysurfer X8
relevance: TU Delft flight-test thesis that identifies longitudinal Skysurfer X8 dynamics from real elevator/throttle sweeps and doublets, then compares identified frequency responses/state-space dynamics with XFLR5. The modified test article is 1.41 m span and 0.915 m long, with two wing-mounted motors, Pixhawk 4/PX4, IMU, GPS and pitot. It reports 30 m test altitude, 18 m/s trim, 0.4–5 Hz excitation, and logged PWM input/output plus airdata, attitude, rates and accelerations. These distinguish command channels, onboard measurements, and derived transfer/state-space models.
limitations: The two-engine test installation differs materially from the stock single-pusher Skysurfer. Input is actuator PWM command, not measured control-surface angle; states include PX4 estimator outputs. Flight ULogs are described as saved on the controller SD card and converted to MATLAB, but are not included in this thesis or a located public dataset. The thesis reports noisy/poorly excited forward-speed response and difficult trim, so transfer functions should be used with the author-reported fit limits.
access: public TU Delft repository PDF downloaded; full text inspected; underlying logs not published in the thesis
license: Institutional thesis copy; reuse license not stated
read_depth: Full 129-page thesis inspected; airframe modifications, sensor/flight-log schema, maneuver protocol, identification, results and limitations reviewed

title: Determining the lateral-directional handling characteristics of a Skysurfer X8
relevance: Actual flight-test identification of lateral-directional response on a 1.41 m X-UAV Skysurfer X8 with twin counter-rotating motors, Pixhawk 4/custom PX4, GNSS, pitot and four control servos. Rudder and aileron sweeps and a separate validation input sequence are analyzed. Sensor recordings and servo-command inputs are distinct; derived sideslip/wind/state-space quantities are estimates. The thesis reports roll subsidence, Dutch-roll and spiral modes, including an unstable spiral-mode doubling time of 5.18 s and a Dutch-roll frequency of 0.93 Hz.
limitations: The test installation is a modified twin-motor X8 and results are for its configured flight condition. The thesis explains that key control/servo signals were logged at only 5 Hz despite 50 Hz servo/controller updates, limiting high-frequency input fidelity; reported model states and mode metrics are derived from the flight data. The repository does not publish the underlying flight logs, only figures and analyzed results. Reuse rights are unavailable in repository metadata. This is a separate lateral-directional thesis from the related Juffermans longitudinal thesis; the pair may share the same X8 flight-test program.
access: public TU Delft repository thesis downloaded; full text inspected; raw flight logs not present
license: Reuse rights not available in repository metadata
read_depth: Full 132-page thesis inspected; abstract, test-aircraft configuration, sensors, controller/logging rates, flight maneuvers, identification, validation and reported mode characteristics checked

title: System Identification of Flexible Aircraft: Lessons Learned from the X-56A Phase 1 Flight Tests
relevance: NASA's Phase 1 program flew the X-56A in 39 flights and about 1,000 research maneuvers from 2017–2019. The paper estimates rigid-body and structural-mode frequency responses and nondimensional stability/control derivatives from actual flight-test data. It documents 18 accelerometers, 24 strain gauges, a fiber-optic strain sensor, high-bandwidth gyros, surface string potentiometers, and boom air-data measurements (airspeed, angle of attack, sideslip). Inputs were multisine excitations inserted after the active flight-control law and mixer; measured surface positions, rather than commands alone, entered the identification.
limitations: The X-56A is a large subscale aeroelastic research aircraft (about 28 ft span; configuration-dependent 200–480 lb), not a hobby RC model. Its wings are structurally flexible, not actively morphing. This paper reports methods, estimates and selected measured traces, but does not release the underlying flight logs or complete numeric coefficient tables as a reusable dataset. Results are for its documented configurations and envelope.
access: Public NASA NTRS conference-paper PDF; locally downloaded. NASA identifies the work as U.S. Government work with public use permitted.
license: U.S. Government work; NTRS states Public Use Permitted.
read_depth: Full PDF downloaded and parsed; flight program, sensors, sampling/reprocessing semantics, excitation path and estimation methods reviewed. No independent re-estimation performed.

title: Data from: Bird-inspired reflexive morphing enables rudderless flight
relevance: The Dryad record describes raw measurements for 81 combinations of wing/tail morph, angle of attack, actuator mixing and turbulence. `WindTunnelTrials.mat` contains attitude, raw servo outputs, airspeed, IMU, yaw/pitch/roll PID traces and trial indexing; open-loop, yaw-damper and turbulence cases are distinguished. The associated physical model PigeonBot II uses morphing feathered wings and tail without a vertical tail. Useful for force/moment response, actuator coupling and stability trends in a morphing vehicle.
limitations: This dataset is wind-tunnel ‘virtual flight’ data, not an unconstrained outdoor free-flight log. Attitude data are from the onboard autopilot; it is not a motion-capture 6-DOF validation record. The 248,583,985-byte MAT file is too large to inspect within this pass; the official Dryad API listed SHA-256 but its download endpoint returned HTTP 401 and the file-stream endpoint HTTP 403, so that checksum is not locally verified and no raw file is retained. Treat its biohybrid bird geometry, tunnel support, and test conditions as model-specific.
access: Public Dryad record, CC0-1.0. Metadata reports 366,371,318 bytes total; `WindTunnelTrials.mat` is 248,583,985 bytes. Direct download attempts returned HTTP 401/403; no access-control workaround was attempted.
license: CC0-1.0 (Dryad API metadata).
read_depth: Dryad record/API metadata and its data dictionary reviewed; associated Science Robotics article and described experiment reviewed. Raw MAT structure and numeric values not inspected because the public file endpoint rejected direct retrieval.

title: Dataset for: Airspeed estimation for UAVs using only propeller feedback
relevance: The 4TU-repository-linked TU Delft author repository contains the experimental inputs for Ntouros et al.'s Cyclone tailsitter study. `data/input/training.mat` and `test.mat` each contain processed flight arrays with 55,000 and 43,500 samples respectively: corrected Pitot airspeed, right-ESC RPM/voltage/current, body angular rates, Euler angles, N/E/D GPS velocity and time (about 110 s and 87 s). Both files declare `fs=500` and have uniform 2 ms timestamp spacing, so 500 Hz is the stored grid; the paper does not establish it as an independent sensor hardware clock. The paper describes manual flights with turns and speed/altitude changes on a 1.00 kg, 0.90 m-span tailsitter with two tractor props; airspeed is corrected for the right propeller's 0.24 m lateral offset using body roll rate. The repository separately includes `wt.mat` (254,500 samples of physical propeller/ESC wind-tunnel measurements) and `BEM.mat` (10,000 simulated propeller points); these are not flight records.
limitations: The MATLAB files are processed arrays, not original PX4/SD-log or onboard raw telemetry; flight logs include no explicit pilot/control-surface command channel. The stored 500 Hz grid should not be described as a verified independent hardware sampling clock. The model's principal airspeed-fit regime is forward flight (advance ratio above the paper's Jcrit=0.20); the authors note nominal small-angle assumptions and do not validate all hover/high-angle behavior. The separate wind-tunnel and BEM records must not be represented as flight tests.
access: Public 4TU dataset record links the author-maintained TU Delft GitHub repository. Acquired an immutable repository snapshot at commit 6db5cc19327f0d6c31a4e51783a442704007dbc; ZIP CRCs passed. MAT structures and numeric dimensions were inspected without executing repository code. Repository's CC-BY-4.0 data license is included in the archive.
license: CC-BY-4.0 for data (repository LICENSES/CC-BY-4.0.txt); repository code is separately GPL-3.0.
read_depth: 4TU record, linked GitHub README/license, and associated final journal article reviewed. All four `data/input/*.mat` members were CRC-checked, identified as MATLAB v5 numeric structs, and inspected for fields, dimensions, sampling rate, time range and numeric bounds; no repository code was run.

Use the linked dataset for numerical records; figures in the article alone are not a substitute for raw flight logs.

title: Experiments in Fixed-Wing UAV Perching
relevance: An unusually rich small-aircraft physical study: a 77 g, 98 mm-chord glider performed aggressive post-stall approaches to a string perch. The authors report 240 real flight trajectories for identification. A 16-camera Vicon MX system reconstructed aircraft/elevator kinematics at about 119 Hz with sub-mm marker accuracy; the hand-tuned elevator policy was evaluated by a 50 Hz ground station using communicated motion-capture state. The paper derives aerodynamic coefficients from unsteady measured flight kinematics rather than a tunnel-only model.
limitations: The glider has no onboard power plant. State sensing and feedback control are offboard in an indoor motion-capture arena; it is not an onboard avionics or free-flight navigation log. The paper gives the trajectory processing and selected results but no reusable raw 240-trial numeric file was located. Treat its high-AoA model and perch dynamics as this model/facility's evidence, not a generic RC polar.
access: Public author-hosted PDF copy; full paper downloaded. No explicit open-content reuse license was located.
license: Publisher copyright; author-hosted copy, reuse license not stated.
read_depth: Full 12-page PDF downloaded and parsed; aircraft dimensions/mass, 240-trial dataset semantics, Vicon marker/state accuracy, sample/update rates, filtering and control loop reviewed.

title: NeuroBEM: Hybrid Aerodynamic Quadrotor Model — held-out flight data segment
relevance: A 400 Hz real-flight data segment from the NeuroBEM custom quadrotor, part of a 96-flight 1 h 15 min dataset with states and individual motor speeds. The official README reports 0.772 kg mass and diagonal inertia [0.0025, 0.0021, 0.0043] kg m^2. The selected maneuver is the 2021-02-18-13-44-23 test-set segment 2; it provides actual numeric state and motor-speed response useful for flight dynamics and rotor-response comparisons.
limitations: Not a conventional RC helicopter or EDF/turbine airplane. The processed CSV has no raw IMU channels, no target motor commands, and no direct thrust/torque measurement. Position/pose are Vicon; velocity, acceleration, body rates and angular accelerations are filtered or derived using Vicon and onboard measurements. The data represents one custom 0.772 kg quadrotor and should not be scaled directly to a different rotor/airframe.
access: Public download from the University of Zurich Robotics and Perception Group project page. One selected CSV was extracted via HTTP byte ranges from the published processed_data.zip; the full 627 MB archive was not retained. ZIP CRC32 validated by Python zipfile while extracting.
license: Not stated for the dataset on the project page or README; preserve attribution and confirm terms before redistribution.
read_depth: Official project page and dataset README read; paper inspected; selected CSV header, sample and complete ZIP member CRC checked.

title: Nonlinear System Identification for a Nano-drone Benchmark — Crazyflie 2.1 Brushless held-out Melon run
type: real-flight system-identification dataset and journal study
relevance: Real 100 Hz Crazyflie 2.1 Brushless flight log, one held-out Melon trajectory run from a 15-flight nonlinear identification benchmark. The CSV has 6,500 rows with time, position, velocity, quaternion attitude, body rates, four per-motor angular velocities, and body specific acceleration. The paper documents a 45 g vehicle with diagonal inertia [2.3951e-5, 2.3951e-5, 3.2347e-5] kg m^2; the speed inputs are ESC sensorless back-EMF telemetry, a physically closer actuator signal than a high-level thrust setpoint.
limitations: Not a conventional helicopter or fixed-wing EDF/turbine. The flight is closed-loop tracking in a 6 x 6 x 2.5 m OptiTrack room; no direct force/torque sensors and no raw motor PWM or pilot RC inputs are in this CSV. Position, attitude and velocity use mixed OptiTrack/laser/optical-flow sources; body rates are gyro readings and specific acceleration is accelerometer output. The paper aligns, resamples to 100 Hz and applies zero-phase low-pass filtering to continuous signals. The nano-scale motor/prop/airframe regime does not scale directly to larger models.
access: Public LFS object from the authors’ GitHub repository. The binary downloaded at the official media URL matches the repository LFS pointer’s SHA-256 OID and declared size.
license: No data-specific license found in the authors’ GitHub repository. ETH Research Collection identifies the published article as CC BY 4.0; do not assume that status applies to the separate CSV.
read_depth: Published article methods and dataset table read; repository README and LFS pointer checked; full numeric CSV parsed for row width, finite values, time span and cadence.

title: DronePropA: Motion Trajectories Dataset for Commercial Drones with Defective Propellers — QDrone 2 healthy fast cross run 1
relevance: A healthy, high-speed cross-trajectory run from the public DronePropA dataset. This 1 kHz QDrone 2 log contains 87,837 samples across commander, onboard vehicle, and stabilizer arrays. The data article specifies a 1.5 kg maximum takeoff weight for the QDrone 2 platform and describes reference trajectory/controller signals, two onboard IMUs, battery and altitude data, and four per-motor command and ESC outputs. It gives real motion, sensor, and actuator-command data from a commercial flight controller.
limitations: A commercial multirotor rather than an RC helicopter or fixed-wing EDF/turbine. The selected flight is a healthy, indoor, closed-loop tracked maneuver without ambient wind. The paper identifies controller and motor/ESC command outputs, not direct thrust/torque or measured rotor RPM; the position/yaw fields combine trajectory references and OptiTrack data, while accelerations and angular rates come from onboard IMUs. The platform and controller differ from a model-aircraft propulsion system, so scaling is not direct.
access: Public Mendeley Data download; selected original MATLAB v5 file obtained through the official dataset API. File size and SHA-256 match the API metadata; MAT variables and dimensions inspected without executing code.
license: CC BY 4.0 (Mendeley Data record).
read_depth: Mendeley dataset record and Data in Brief article methods and signal table read; local MATLAB v5 header, variable names/shapes, file size, and source SHA-256 checked.
